title: HLA Genes, Expression and Minor Antigens: 6p21 Haplotypes, β2-Microglobulin, HLA-C, -E and -G
summary: Locate the MHC at 6p21 and β2-microglobulin on chromosome 15, describe class I and class II structure, predict sibling HLA identity from haplotype inheritance, explain low HLA-C expression and cytokine induction of class I, contrast nonclassical HLA-E and HLA-G, and see why minor antigens such as HA-1 can cause GVHD after an HLA-identical sibling transplant.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 50 Hits 1 (6p21, haplotypes, 1-in-4 sibling identity), 3 (class I and II structure, β2-microglobulin on chromosome 15), 8 (HLA-C low expression, cytokine induction of class I), 11 (minor histocompatibility antigens, HA-1), 12 (HLA-E and HLA-G) and Trap 4 (β2-microglobulin not in the MHC). Checked against Choo 2007, Zemmour 1992, McCutcheon 1995 (abstract only), Kaur 2017, Crux 2017, Lucas 2025, Hunt 2006, Rebmann 2014, Shukla 2021, Neumann 1997, Leeuwenberg 1987, Sellami 2010 and Han 2025. Hit 12 states HLA-G protection of the placenta as settled; Hunt 2006 says most of that evidence is associative (register rv-hlag-tolerance-evidence). The Number Vault attributes low HLA-C expression to inefficient association and a mutated enhancer; McCutcheon 1995 found β2-microglobulin association comparable to HLA-A and -B and linked low expression to faster mRNA turnover (register rv-hla-c-expression-mechanism). The reviewer gives the heavy chain as 44 kDa; the source read gives about 45 kD, so the lesson says “about 45 kDa”. Not taught as fact: class II chain weights (33–35/26–28 kDa), class I absence on muscle and sperm (only rat neurons were checked), HLA-C enhancer mechanism.

objectives: Locate the MHC and the β2-microglobulin gene and describe class I and class II molecular structure.
Predict the chance that two siblings are HLA-identical from haplotype inheritance.
Describe HLA-C surface expression, cytokine induction of class I, and the roles of HLA-E and HLA-G.
Explain how minor histocompatibility antigens can cause GVHD after an HLA-identical sibling transplant.

scenes.title: One family, two questions
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: a family is HLA-typed because one child needs a stem-cell transplant. Father carries haplotypes a and b, mother c and d; the patient is a/c. Two siblings are tested. Brother is a/c (HLA-identical); sister is b/c (shares one haplotype). After transplant from the HLA-identical brother, the patient still develops acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Question tokens: “What were the odds of an identical sibling?” and “Why GVHD with an identical match?”

cues.text: A family is typed because one child needs a stem-cell transplant. Father carries haplotypes a and b; mother carries c and d; the patient is a and c.
The brother is also a and c: HLA-identical. The sister shares only one haplotype. The brother donates, yet the patient still develops graft-versus-host disease.
What were the odds of an identical sibling, and why can an identical HLA match still cause GVHD?

scenes.title: Where the genes are, how the molecules are built
scenes.altText: Schematic chromosome 6 with the MHC at 6p21, split into class I (HLA-A, -B, -C), class II (DR, DQ, DP) and class III (complement C2, C4, factor B, TNF; no HLA molecules). Class I molecule: a glycosylated heavy chain (three extracellular domains α1, α2, α3, a transmembrane region and a cytoplasmic tail; about 45 kDa) noncovalently bound to β2-microglobulin, an invariant ~12-kDa protein encoded on chromosome 15 (15q21). Class II molecule: an α chain and a β chain, both transmembrane; α1 and β1 form the peptide groove.

cues.text: The human MHC sits on the short arm of chromosome 6, at 6p21. Its class I region holds HLA-A, B and C; its class II region holds DR, DQ and DP; and its class III region holds complement and TNF genes, not HLA molecules.
A class I molecule is a heavy chain with three outer domains, alpha one to three, plus a transmembrane anchor. Alpha one and alpha two form the peptide groove.
The heavy chain is paired, without a covalent bond, to beta-2 microglobulin: a small, invariant protein of about twelve kilodaltons encoded on chromosome 15, outside the MHC.
A class II molecule is two chains, alpha and beta, and both cross the membrane. Alpha one and beta one together build the groove.

scenes.title: Where HLA is expressed, and the nonclassical molecules
scenes.altText: Expression card: class I on almost all nucleated cells; class II on B cells, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells and activated T cells. HLA-C reaches the surface at about 10% of HLA-A and -B levels; one study linked this to faster HLA-C mRNA degradation, while β2-microglobulin association was comparable. Induction card: IFN-γ raises class I, β2-microglobulin and TAP (via NLRC5); TNF-α raises class I through autocrine IFN-β. In a rat neuron study, no constitutive surface class I was detected until IFN-γ induced it. HLA-E: least polymorphic class I, presents leader peptides of other class I molecules to inhibitory CD94/NKG2A on NK cells. HLA-G: few alleles, found on extravillous cytotrophoblast; trophoblast lacks HLA-A, -B and class II but expresses HLA-C; HLA-G binds inhibitory ILT2/ILT4; its tolerance role rests mostly on associative evidence.

cues.text: Class I is on almost all nucleated cells; class II is limited to B cells, antigen-presenting cells and activated T cells. HLA-C reaches the cell surface at only about a tenth of HLA-A and B levels.

Inflammation turns expression up. Interferon gamma raises class I, beta-2 microglobulin and the TAP transporter; TNF alpha raises class I through interferon beta. In a rat study, neurons showed no surface class I until interferon gamma induced it.

HLA-E is a nonclassical class I molecule with little polymorphism. It mostly presents leader peptides cut from other class I molecules, and that complex engages the inhibitory receptor CD94 NKG2A, calming NK cells. NK cells attack cells that lose class I: missing self.

HLA-G has few alleles and was found on extravillous cytotrophoblast. Trophoblast lacks HLA-A, B and class II but keeps HLA-C. HLA-G binds inhibitory receptors, and is linked to maternal tolerance, though much of that evidence is associative.

scenes.title: Haplotypes and minor antigens
scenes.altText: Family table: haplotypes a/b × c/d give four possible children (a/c, a/d, b/c, b/d). Any two siblings: 25% HLA-identical, 50% haploidentical, 25% share no haplotype. Minor histocompatibility antigens: peptides from polymorphic proteins encoded outside the MHC and inherited independently of it. HA-1 is a nonapeptide from the HMHA1 gene on 19p13, presented by HLA-A*02:01/02:06; in a 60-pair Tunisian study of HLA-genoidentical sibling transplants, HA-1 disparity was associated with acute GVHD. Hook answers: 1 in 4 odds; GVHD from a minor-antigen mismatch is one possible explanation.

cues.text: HLA genes are tightly linked, so each parent passes on a whole haplotype. Two parents with haplotypes a, b and c, d can produce four combinations.
Any two siblings therefore have a twenty-five percent chance of being HLA-identical, fifty percent of sharing one haplotype, and twenty-five percent of sharing none.

Minor histocompatibility antigens are encoded outside the MHC and inherited independently. HA-1, for example, comes from the HMHA1 gene on chromosome 19. A mismatch for HA-1 between HLA-identical siblings has been associated with acute GVHD.
Back to the hook: one in four odds for an identical sibling, and a minor-antigen mismatch is one way an identical HLA match can still cause GVHD.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “The β2-microglobulin gene is in the MHC on chromosome 6” (✓ it is on chromosome 15, outside the MHC); “An HLA-identical sibling donor cannot cause GVHD” (✓ minor histocompatibility antigens, encoded outside the MHC, can still be mismatched); “HLA-E is just another classical antigen-presenting molecule” (✓ it mostly presents class I leader peptides to inhibitory CD94/NKG2A on NK cells).

cues.text: Trap one: the beta-2 microglobulin gene sits in the MHC on chromosome 6. No: it is on chromosome 15.
Trap two: an HLA-identical sibling cannot cause GVHD. No: minor histocompatibility antigens, encoded outside the MHC, can still differ.
Trap three: HLA-E presents peptides like HLA-A and B. No: it mostly shows class I leader peptides to CD94 NKG2A, inhibiting NK cells.

scenes.title: Headquarters, sidekick, outsiders
scenes.altText: Memory aid: the MHC is HEADQUARTERS on 6p21, passed to each child as a whole building (haplotype); β2-microglobulin is the SIDEKICK who lives on chromosome 15 and commutes in; minor antigens are OUTSIDERS from elsewhere in the genome (HA-1 on chromosome 19) who can still start a fight. Tokens: HQ = 6p21 · sidekick = 15 · outsiders = minor antigens. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the MHC is headquarters on 6p21, handed to each child as a whole building. Beta-2 microglobulin is the sidekick who lives on chromosome 15 and commutes in. Minor antigens are outsiders from elsewhere in the genome who can still start a fight.

Where it breaks: recombination inside the MHC occasionally splits a haplotype; there are many minor antigens on many chromosomes, not one address; and the sidekick is essential, because class I needs beta-2 microglobulin to reach the surface.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “MHC 6p21 · haplotypes · siblings 25% identical · β2m on 15”, “HLA-C ~10% · HLA-E → CD94/NKG2A · minor antigens outside MHC → GVHD”.

cues.text: HLA genes travel together as 6p21 haplotypes, so two siblings match one time in four, while beta-2 microglobulin comes from chromosome 15, HLA-C sits at about a tenth of HLA-A and HLA-B levels, HLA-E calms NK cells, and minor antigens encoded outside the MHC can still cause GVHD.

props.label: MHC 6p21 · haplotypes · siblings 25% identical · β2m on 15
HLA-C ~10% · HLA-E → CD94/NKG2A · minor antigens → GVHD

explanation.what: Plain language: the HLA genes sit together on chromosome 6 and are inherited as a block from each parent, so siblings often match each other. The class I molecule borrows a small partner protein, β2-microglobulin, made from a gene on a different chromosome. Some HLA molecules are expressed weakly (HLA-C), some are switched up by inflammation, and two nonclassical ones (HLA-E and HLA-G) mainly tell NK cells and other immune cells to stand down. Genes outside the MHC can still make mismatched “minor” antigens. Scientific terms: major histocompatibility complex (MHC), 6p21, class I/II/III regions, haplotype, linkage, heavy chain, α1–α3 domains, β2-microglobulin (15q21), class II α and β chains, IFN-γ, NLRC5, TAP, TNF-α, HLA-E, CD94/NKG2A, missing self, HLA-G, extravillous cytotrophoblast, ILT2/ILT4, minor histocompatibility antigen, HA-1 (HMHA1), graft-versus-host disease (GVHD).
explanation.why: Because the MHC is inherited as haplotypes, an HLA-identical sibling is the best-matched stem-cell donor, yet the rest of the genome still differs, so minor antigens can drive GVHD. Expression level and inducibility decide how visible a cell is to T cells and NK cells: HLA-C is low on the surface, inflammation raises class I, and HLA-E complexes inhibit NK cells through CD94/NKG2A.
explanation.measure: Siblings: 25% HLA-identical, 50% haploidentical, 25% no shared haplotype. β2-microglobulin: invariant, about 12 kDa, chromosome 15 (15q21). Class I heavy chain about 45 kDa. HLA-C surface expression about 10% of HLA-A and -B. HA-1 gene HMHA1 on 19p13.
explanation.differs: Class I (heavy chain + β2-microglobulin, nearly all nucleated cells) vs class II (α + β both transmembrane, B cells, antigen-presenting cells, activated T cells); classical HLA-A/-B (broad peptide repertoire, very polymorphic) vs HLA-E (leader peptides, little polymorphism) vs HLA-G (few alleles, trophoblast); major (HLA) vs minor (non-MHC) histocompatibility antigens.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: the chromosome for β2-microglobulin, the probability of an HLA-identical sibling, the HLA locus with the weakest surface expression, the receptor HLA-E engages, where HLA-G is found, or why GVHD occurs after an HLA-identical sibling transplant.

questions.stem: Parents type as haplotypes a/b and c/d. What is the chance that any two of their children are HLA-identical to each other?

options.rationale: Correct. Each child inherits one of four haplotype combinations, so two siblings share both haplotypes one time in four.
Incorrect. 50% is the chance of sharing exactly one haplotype (haploidentical).
Incorrect. Only identical twins are guaranteed to be HLA-identical; siblings receive independent haplotypes.
Incorrect. Because the MHC is inherited as a block, the loci are not assorted separately; the chance is 25%.

questions.stem: A patient receives stem cells from an HLA-identical sibling and develops acute graft-versus-host disease. Which explanation is most consistent with the sources?

options.text: A mismatch in a minor histocompatibility antigen, such as HA-1, encoded outside the MHC
options.rationale: Correct. Minor antigens are inherited independently of the MHC, and HA-1 disparity has been associated with acute GVHD after HLA-identical sibling transplants.

options.text: A β2-microglobulin mismatch at the MHC on chromosome 6
options.rationale: Incorrect. β2-microglobulin is invariant and is encoded on chromosome 15, not in the MHC.

options.text: An HLA-A mismatch missed because siblings cannot share haplotypes
options.rationale: Incorrect. Siblings can share both haplotypes; this donor was HLA-identical.

options.text: Lack of HLA-C on the donor cells
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-C is expressed at lower levels than HLA-A and -B, but it is not absent, and identical siblings share their HLA-C alleles.

options.text: It mostly presents leader peptides of other class I molecules and engages inhibitory CD94/NKG2A on NK cells
options.rationale: Correct. HLA-E bound to class I leader peptides binds CD94/NKG2A with higher affinity than NKG2C, inhibiting NK-cell cytotoxicity.

options.text: It is the most polymorphic HLA locus and a main target of transplant antibodies
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-E is the least polymorphic of the class I molecules.

options.text: It is a class II molecule found only on B cells
options.rationale: Incorrect. HLA-E is a nonclassical class I molecule with broad tissue distribution.

options.text: It is the β2-microglobulin partner of HLA-A and -B
options.rationale: Incorrect. β2-microglobulin is a separate invariant protein encoded on chromosome 15.

claims.text: MHC at 6p21 with class I, II and III regions; class III holds complement and TNF genes, not HLA molecules.
Class I heavy chain (α1–α3, transmembrane, about 45 kDa) noncovalently paired with invariant β2-microglobulin (about 12 kDa, chromosome 15q21); class II α and β both transmembrane, groove α1 + β1.
MHC inherited as haplotypes; two siblings 25% identical, 50% haploidentical, 25% no shared haplotype.

Class I on almost all nucleated cells; class II on B cells, antigen-presenting cells and activated T cells; HLA-C surface expression about 10% of HLA-A and -B, linked in one study to faster mRNA turnover with comparable β2-microglobulin association.
IFN-γ raises class I, β2-microglobulin and TAP (via NLRC5); TNF-α raises class I through autocrine IFN-β; rat neurons showed no constitutive surface class I until IFN-γ induction.
HLA-E: least polymorphic class I, presents class I leader peptides, engages inhibitory CD94/NKG2A; NK cells kill cells that lose class I (missing self).
HLA-G: few alleles, on extravillous cytotrophoblast; trophoblast lacks HLA-A, -B and class II but expresses HLA-C; ligand for ILT2/ILT4; tolerance role mostly supported by associative evidence.
Minor histocompatibility antigens are inherited independently of the MHC; HA-1 (HMHA1, 19p13) disparity associated with acute GVHD after HLA-identical sibling transplant.

Reviewer’s class II chain weights (α 33–35 kDa, β 26–28 kDa) and exact 44-kDa heavy chain; class I undetectable on muscle and sperm; HLA-C low expression from “inefficient association + mutated enhancer A”.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 50 Hit 12 states that HLA-G protects the placenta and underlies maternofetal tolerance as settled fact. Hunt 2006 notes that most reports of HLA-G-mediated tolerance are associative rather than clearly illustrative of definitive function, so the lesson teaches HLA-G as linked to tolerance (register rv-hlag-tolerance-evidence).

Ch. 50 Number Vault attributes the roughly 10-fold lower HLA-C expression to “inefficient association + mutated enhancer A”. McCutcheon 1995 found HLA-C heavy chains associate with β2-microglobulin at rates comparable to HLA-A and -B and linked low expression to faster mRNA turnover; Kaur 2017 lists inefficient peptide binding or chaperone association only as proposals. The lesson teaches the about-10% level without a settled mechanism (register rv-hla-c-expression-mechanism).
